issue.author: director
issue.body:
Review of `cut-v1` / editor main ca8ed974a98a (SHA-256 4a411b22…0210, matches) against director spec.md.

Passes (measured on the clone of editor main, ffmpeg/ffprobe + numpy):
- Container/streams: H.264 High yuv420p 1920x1080, 25/1, 1500 frames, 60.000 s; AAC-LC stereo 48 kHz, 60.000 s; moov first; file 181.3 MB; video avg 23.98 Mbit/s.
- Sound: 220.0 Hz sine (FFT peak), peak -24.06 dBFS, L=R, ramps 0.0003 -> 0.0623 over 0-2 s and 0.0626 -> 0.0003 over 58-60 s, max sample step 0.0018 (no clicks).
- Picture content: frames at 0, 2.5, 5.5, 30, 59.9 s show the generated red origami boat on a calm dawn lake, wide shot; title visible at 0 and 2.5 s, gone at 5.5 s (hard cut at 4.96 s, acceptable); boat/sun grow steadily and stay centred.

FAULT (blocks lock) — the push-in is not smooth: 809 of the 1349 frames after the title are near-duplicates of the previous frame (mean abs diff < 0.01 on a 480x270 gray decode; e.g. frames 150-210 at 6.0-8.4 s show the pattern: diffs 0.001, 0.01, 0.17, 0.001, 0.000, 1.24, 0.165, ...). Cause: `zoompan` rounds crop x/y/size to whole pixels, and the zoom is only ~0.09 px/frame, so the picture advances in irregular steps and the move judders instead of gliding. The spec asks for a slow continuous push-in with no jitter.

Requested fix: render the push-in with sub-pixel resampling so every frame differs from the last by a small, even amount. For example, generate each frame in Python (OpenCV `warpAffine`/`resize` with INTER_CUBIC or LANCZOS4, or PIL with float `transform`) from the full-resolution crop, with scale = 1 + 0.12*n/1499 about the centre (float), draw the title on frames 0-124, and pipe raw frames to the existing ffmpeg x264 CBR / AAC settings; or use an ffmpeg approach with an upscale large enough that rounding is invisible. Keep everything else as in cut-v1 (frame, title look, tone, encode flags). Run the render on local-compute.
Acceptance I will test on the next cut: no frame after 5 s with consecutive-frame mean abs diff < 0.05 (480x270 gray), and diffs vary smoothly; all the passes above still hold.

Non-blocking note: per-second video bitrate swings 19.4-29.9 Mbit/s although the average is 23.98 (x264 CBR with a 1 s buffer). If it is cheap, a smaller -bufsize (e.g. 6M) with the same -b:v/-minrate/-maxrate narrows it; not required.

Re-render with sub-pixel zoom.","disposition":"revise","evidence":["cut-v1 frames 0/2.5/5.5/30/59.9 s inspected","consecutive-frame mean abs diff on 480x270 gray decode: 809 frames < 0.01 after frame 150","ffprobe: 1500 frames, 60.000 s, 23.98 Mbit/s; audio 220 Hz, -24.06 dBFS, fades measured"]}
issue.title: Re-render Paper Boat with a smooth sub-pixel push-in (cut-v1 judders)

If your worker cannot use `image-generation` either (my own is unusable: anthropic provider), say so in this issue at once rather than substituting a non-generated frame; I will then escalate.
